The August 28 statement from the student body recognises the importance of the Chief Justice of India's (CJI) association with the convocation given that he is the ex-officio Chancellor of NLSIU. However, it argues that at the same time, concerns and views expressed by graduating students should not have resulted in the cancellation of the convocation itself. "A graduating batch must have the autonomy and freedom to express its collective views on matters concerning its convocation, including regarding the invitation of guests to the ceremony. Administrative authority over the conduct of a convocation cannot extend to controlling the substance of students' collective expression," it says. The statement notes that NLSIU occupies a significant place in the Indian legal education landscape and remains the institution that countless aspiring law students dream of attending. items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Saturday ordered the State Director General of Police (DGP) to issue guidelines with regard to the cases registered over social media posts [Mohan Gowda v. State of Karnataka] . Justice M Nagaprasanna referred to the case of Nalla Balu v State of Telangana in which Telangana High Court's guidelines on handling complaints made with respect to social media posts were upheld by the Supreme Court. "The High Court of Telangana had directed verification of locus standi at the outset, preliminary inquiry to be conducted and a higher threshold of these two to be met for media post or speech related offences. items.title: Parandur Airport ரத்து: முதலீடுகளுக்கு ஆபத்தா? | CM Vijay | TN Assembly | Shabbir Ahmed | TNM Tamil
items.summary: The Tamil Nadu government’s decision to drop the proposed greenfield airport at Parandur has opened up a larger debate on the state’s development priorities. The project, estimated to cost around Rs 20,000 crore and planned across thousands of acres, had faced sustained opposition from farmers and residents over land acquisition and its impact on agricultural and water resources. The TVK's decision has drawn sharp criticism from the DMK and BJP, arguing that scrapping a major infrastructure project could hurt Tamil Nadu’s industrial growth, employment and ability to attract investments. So, does Tamil Nadu really need a new international airport? What does the data on passenger traffic and existing airport capacity tell us? And is the claim that scrapping Parandur will cost Tamil Nadu investments backed by evidence? In this week’s episode of Yen Endra Kelvi, Shabbir Ahmed examines the Parandur airport debate, explains the stats around the existing airport and on how Tamil Nadu’s growth future would look like.
